purpose: Identify the first genuinely nonlinear local atom in the Hamiltonian-cycle plus complementary-2-factor tension carrier. Complementary triangles collapse to one signed GF(3) arc variable with linear equalities; complementary 4-cycles produce the six-state EXACT2_4 signature, which is not affine over GF(3). This matches the source-backed transition from the cycle-plus-triangles theorem to NP-hard fixed complementary cycle length at least four.

setup.graph: Let G be a graph with a fixed oriented Hamiltonian cycle H and let Q=(u_1,...,u_k,u_1) be one cycle component of E(G)\E(H).
setup.tension: Let t in GF(3)^{E(H)} be the nonzero Hamiltonian-edge tension induced by a proper 3-colouring.
setup.arc_sums: For each j, let a_j be the oriented sum of t along the H-arc from u_j to u_{j+1}, using the cyclic order of the Q vertices and the chosen H orientation. Equivalently a_j=c(u_{j+1})-c(u_j).
setup.local_properness: The Q edge u_j u_{j+1} is proper iff a_j!=0. Telescoping around Q gives sum_j a_j=0 in GF(3).

triangle_theorem.name: COMPLEMENTARY_TRIANGLE_TENSION_SIGNATURE_IS_ONE_SIGN
triangle_theorem.statement: For k=3, Q is properly coloured iff (a_1,a_2,a_3) is (1,1,1) or (-1,-1,-1). Equivalently a_1=a_2=a_3!=0.
proof: Nonzero GF(3) values are exactly +1 and -1.
Three signs sum to zero mod 3 iff all three are +1 or all three are -1; every mixed pattern has sum +1 or -1.
Hence the triangle contributes only one binary orientation sign tau_Q with linear equations a_1=a_2=a_3=tau_Q and tau_Q!=0.
triangle_theorem.interpretation: This explains algebraically why complementary triangles are exceptional: their local nowhere-zero cycle condition does not create a multi-state nonlinear relation beyond one nonzero scalar.

four_cycle_theorem.name: COMPLEMENTARY_C4_TENSION_SIGNATURE_IS_EXACT2_4
four_cycle_theorem.statement: For k=4, Q is properly coloured iff exactly two of a_1,...,a_4 equal +1 and exactly two equal -1. The local feasible signature therefore has exactly binom(4,2)=6 states.
proof: Write r for the number of +1 entries. Then sum_j a_j = r-(4-r)=2r-4 in GF(3).
The equation 2r-4=0 mod 3 with 0<=r<=4 has the unique solution r=2.
Thus proper C4 tension is exactly the balanced two-plus/two-minus relation.
four_cycle_theorem.nonaffine_corollary: The six feasible sign vectors cannot be an affine subspace or affine coset over GF(3): every nonempty affine GF(3) set has cardinality 3^d, whereas 6 is not a power of three.

general_cycle_count.formula: For a complementary k-cycle the local sign patterns are s in {+1,-1}^k with sum s_j=0 mod 3. If r is the number of +1 signs, feasibility is 2r-k=0 mod 3.
general_cycle_count.meaning: k=3 is the first degenerate linearizable case; k=4 is the first case with a six-state nonaffine signature.

source_backed_boundary.positive_side: The Fleischner-Stiebitz cycle-plus-triangles theorem states that a Hamiltonian cycle plus a vertex-disjoint triangle 2-factor is always 3-colourable (indeed 3-choosable).
source_backed_boundary.search_firewall: Known proofs are non-algorithmic, and the complexity of finding a proper 3-colouring of a cycle-plus-triangles graph remains open in the cited algorithmic literature; therefore this artifact does not claim a polynomial witness-construction terminal for the triangle-only case.
source_backed_boundary.hard_side: Fleischner-Sabidussi prove NP-completeness for 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs even when every complementary component is a non-selfcrossing cycle of one fixed length at least four.
source_backed_boundary.alignment: The first local nonaffine tension signature appears exactly at length four, matching the first source-backed hard complementary-cycle regime.

positive: Complementary triangle constraints may be replaced exactly by one nonzero GF(3) sign plus linear arc-equality equations.
The degree-four Hamiltonian frontier can be normalized to a Hamiltonian tension system whose first nonlinear local component is EXACT2_4 on arc sums.
killed: Treat all fixed complementary cycle lengths as equivalent affine GF(3) constraints.
Assume that constant local cycle length alone gives a polynomial solver: hardness persists for every fixed length at least four.
not_killed: A source-specific polynomial contraction for coupled EXACT2_4 arc signatures exploiting Hamiltonian interval overlap.
A Pfaffian/matroid/minimax representation of the global balanced-sign system.
A constructive polynomial algorithm for cycle-plus-triangles search.

next_target.name: E8_HAMILTONIAN_EXACT2_4_ARC_BALANCE_CONTRACTION_V5_4
next_target.directive: Attack 4-regular Hamiltonian sources whose complementary components are 4-cycles. Replace each component by its exact six-state two-plus/two-minus arc-sum signature. Seek a polynomial global contraction using interval overlap/crossing structure without enumerating six states per component. Any candidate must reconstruct vertex colours and survive the fixed-C4 NP-hard source firewall.

sources: Fleischner and Stiebitz, cycle-plus-triangles theorem: Hamiltonian cycle plus disjoint triangles is 3-colourable/3-choosable.
Fleischner and Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2), 2003.
Berczi and Kobayashi, An algorithm for identifying cycle-plus-triangles graphs, Discrete Applied Mathematics 226, 2017: recognition is polynomial, while finding a proper 3-colouring is left open.
